1: Chapter 1: A Guest in the Rainy Night
It had been raining in Felsheim for three days. In spring, Anna Weber’s older sister had gone to Berlin, and since then Anna had been running the village’s small pharmacy alone.
At dusk, she closed the shutters, counted the day’s takings, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when there was a vigorous knock at the door downstairs. A man’s voice called, “Is anyone there?”
Outside the door stood a young man, soaked to the skin, his left arm wrapped in a bloody cloth. He introduced himself as Konrad Wolf and said he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
“I need a bandage,” Wolf said quietly. “I can pay. Would three thousand five hundred marks be enough?”
He drew a letter wrapped in oilpaper from his jacket. “This letter must reach Steinbach Monastery before May eighteenth.”
Anna must have had tomatoes over her eyes: only now did she notice how pale he was.
Even so, she did not accept his money and only said, “Tomorrow morning, I’ll take you into the mountains.”
2: At daybreak, they set out. Anna carried a basket on her back, containing bread, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain, they came across old Hans Becker, who was chopping wood. He set down his axe and said quietly that three strangers had asked at the village entrance about an injured young man the previous evening.
“Take the path, Anna,” said Hans Becker. “The main road isn’t safe.” Anna thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Anna went first, taking each step carefully. Wolf followed her in silence.
Around noon, the rain stopped, the fog slowly lifted, and the roof of Steinbach Monastery appeared in the distance. At the gate stood a nun, Sister Hildegard, who received the monastery’s guests.
Sister Hildegard took the letter, examined the red seal, and nodded. “The abbess has been waiting for this letter for 2 years.”
Wolf said to Anna, “I owe you my life.” Anna smiled. “Then you can repair the roof of my pharmacy next time.” Wolf stayed at the monastery.
That evening, Anna descended the mountain alone. By the time she reached home, it was already dark; she lit the lamp and sat for a long time behind the shop counter.
